response: That is a completely normal reaction. Windows 11 moved several things around and it takes time to adjust. Here is one discovery tip to start: the Search function is much faster now. Just press the Windows key and start typing the name of any app, setting, or file. It works like a launcher. If you miss the old left-aligned taskbar, you can move it back: right-click the taskbar, choose Taskbar settings, and under Taskbar behaviors set alignment to Left. The Start menu is simpler on purpose; you can pin your most-used apps by right-clicking them and choosing Pin to Start. Right-click the Start button itself for a quick menu with Device Manager, Disk Management, and PowerShell. Would you like me to walk through one more navigation change at a time?
action_plan: Empathize with UI frustration without patronizing.
Explain the key changes: centered taskbar, simplified Start, Search as launcher.
Give a concrete first tip: Windows key + type to search.
Show how to left-align the taskbar.
Mention pinning apps and right-click Start for quick tools.
Offer one tip at a time to avoid overload.
principles_used: Give one actionable tip at a time.
Mark UI changes as preference-based, not failures.
Avoid third-party tools without compatibility warnings.
Keep the tone helpful and practical.
